samples.summary: New `seg()` guard is incomplete: `encodeURIComponent` does not escape `.`, so a bare `..` identifier still triggers dot-segment resolution — `api-keys revoke ..` issues `DELETE /workspaces/<ws>/`, which matches the workspace-delete route
samples.evidence:
`seg()` (http-client.ts:32) is `encodeURIComponent`, which escapes `/` (`%2F`) but leaves `.` untouched: `encodeURIComponent('..') === '..'`. The comment at http-client.ts:23-30 claims every interpolated identifier is now safe from dot-segment resolution, but a segment that IS exactly `..` still resolves.

Chain: `wafflebase api-keys revoke ..` → api-keys.ts:76 → `revokeApiKey('..')` → http-client.ts:417 builds `${server}/workspaces/${ws}/api-keys/..` → `fetch` (line 418) normalises with the WHATWG parser to `${server}/workspaces/${ws}/` and sends DELETE with the caller's `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` (jsonHeaders). Backend: `packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:57` declares `@Delete('workspaces/:id')` under `JwtAuthGuard`; Nest/Express run with `strict routing` disabled (no `set('strict routing', …)` in packages/backend/src/main.ts:31-41), so the trailing-slash path matches `:id`. `workspace.service.ts:83-92` then deletes the entire workspace (owner + >1 workspace).

So a key-id of `..` — a plausible value when the id comes from a script, an agent, or untrusted data — turns a scoped `revoke` into irreversible destruction of the whole workspace and its documents. The other `..`-reachable endpoints degrade to 404 (no bare `@Delete()`/`@Get()` on `api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId`, no `@Delete(':tabId')`), so `/workspaces/:id` is the one live target. Fix: reject or escape dot segments (e.g. map `.`/`..` to `%2E`/`%2E%2E`, or validate the identifier) rather than relying on `encodeURIComponent` alone.

samples.summary: `--dry-run` preview diverges from the request actually sent for a `..` identifier, and it diverges on exactly the destructive command the preview exists to protect
samples.evidence: `apiKeysUrl(opts, '..')` (api-keys.ts:17) prints `${server}/workspaces/<ws>/api-keys/..` because `seg('..') === '..'` (dry-run.ts:12-14). The live command sends the same string to `fetch`, which normalises it to `${server}/workspaces/<ws>/` — a DELETE that `packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:57` serves as "delete workspace". An operator (or agent) who pre-flights `api-keys revoke ..` is shown a URL under `/api-keys/`, concludes the request is key-scoped, and then executes a workspace deletion. The same no-op applies to every `seg()` in dry-run.ts, so the invariant the header comment states ("the preview is the request") does not hold for `.`/`..` segments.

samples.summary: New encoding tests cover `../../..` and `?` but not the one input where `encodeURIComponent` is a no-op — a segment that is exactly `..` (or `.`)
samples.evidence: The suite asserts `getDocument('../../../admin/users')`, `deleteDocument('doc-1?force=true')`, `getCell('d/1','t/2','A1/../..')` and `revokeApiKey('../../../documents/d1')` — all contain a `/`, which `encodeURIComponent` escapes, so they all pass. No case exercises `getDocument('..')` / `revokeApiKey('..')`, where the escaping is a no-op and the WHATWG parser still climbs a level. The tests therefore certify a guard that is untested on its residual gap, which is the input that reaches `DELETE /workspaces/:id`.

verdict.reason: Verified independently and the finding holds exactly as described. `seg()` at packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:32-34 is a bare `encodeURIComponent`, which escapes `/` but not `.`, so a segment equal to `..` passes through unchanged despite the comment at :20-31 claiming dot-segment safety. `api-keys revoke <key-id>` (packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:65-76) forwards raw argv to `revokeApiKey` with no validation; http-client.ts:417 interpolates it into `${server}/workspaces/${ws}/api-keys/..` and :418 passes the string to `fetch`, whose WHATWG parsing collapses it to `${server}/workspaces/${ws}/` while still sending the caller's `Authorization` header via `jsonHeaders()`. The collapsed path is a live route, not a 404: ApiKeyController is mounted at root-level `workspaces/:workspaceId/api-keys` (packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.controller.ts:17) and WorkspaceController declares `@Delete('workspaces/:id')` in the same root namespace (packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:21,57); no `setGlobalPrefix` exists in packages/backend/src and DEFAULT_SERVER (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:7) carries no path prefix. main.ts:30-79 never sets `strict routing`, so the trailing slash matches `:id`, and workspace.service.ts:83-92 hard-deletes the workspace (the caller is already an owner because api-key.controller.ts:62 requires `assertOwner`). No guard anywhere rejects or escapes dot segments, so neither `not-present` nor `already-guarded` applies; path traversal / unsafe input handling in a credentialed request is squarely in the security lane, and impact (irreversible workspace destruction from an attacker- or script-supplied identifier) is critical.

finding.evidence: `apiKeysUrl(opts, '..')` (api-keys.ts:17) prints `${server}/workspaces/<ws>/api-keys/..` because `seg('..') === '..'` (dry-run.ts:12-14). The live command sends the same string to `fetch`, which normalises it to `${server}/workspaces/<ws>/` — a DELETE that `packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:57` serves as "delete workspace". An operator (or agent) who pre-flights `api-keys revoke ..` is shown a URL under `/api-keys/`, concludes the request is key-scoped, and then executes a workspace deletion. verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out. dry-run.ts:12-14 defines seg() as encodeURIComponent, which leaves a bare `..` untouched (it only escapes `/`), so api-keys.ts:16-17 prints `${server}/workspaces/<ws>/api-keys/..` for `api-keys revoke ..` (preview emitted at api-keys.ts:73). The live path at http-client.ts:415-418 builds the identical string and passes it to fetch, whose WHATWG URL parser resolves the dot-segment, sending `DELETE ${server}/workspaces/<ws>/`. That route exists and is destructive: workspace.controller.ts:57-64 `@Delete('workspaces/:id')` -> `workspaceService.remove`. No global prefix is configured in packages/backend/src (no setGlobalPrefix match), and the frontend uses the same host-relative `/workspaces` base (frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:7), so the CLI URL does reach that controller; Express non-strict routing matches the trailing slash. No guard rejects traversal-shaped key ids: seg() is the only sanitiser on the path, and the repo's own traversal test only covers `../../../documents/d1` (http-client-paths.test.ts:76-82), where escaping works because of the slashes — the bare `..` case is uncovered and unmitigated. The `api-keys` denials in scripts/agent/hunt-probe.mjs:200 gate a separate agent probe tool, not the CLI. In-lane as path traversal plus a safety gate (--dry-run preview) that misrepresents the request it claims to mirror, per the file's own header comment "so the preview is the request" (api-keys.ts:7-12).

finding.summary: The new `seg()` guard is applied to every identifier EXCEPT `config.workspace`, which is still interpolated raw into every request URL — the same traversal vector the change exists to close.
finding.evidence: `seg()` is documented as covering "every interpolated identifier" (http-client.ts:21-32), but `HttpClient.base` (line 98) builds `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}` unencoded, and the API-key routes repeat it at lines 397, 404 and 415 (`${server}/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}/api-keys`). `dry-run.ts:30` and the new `api-keys.ts:16` mirror the same raw interpolation. `workspace` is untrusted-ish input on exactly the same footing as the ids that were fixed: it comes from `--workspace` argv, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE` env, the YAML profile, or `session.activeWorkspace` (resolveConfig, config.ts:96-99/121-126/142-147). Attack: a caller/agent/CI environment that controls `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE=ws-1/../../../admin` (or a poisoned `~/.wafflebase/config.yaml` profile, which is read with no validation at config.ts:169-180) makes `fetch` normalise the dot segments and send the request — with the `Authorization: Bearer <api key|JWT>` header attached by `authHeaders` (line 73-83) — to an arbitrary path on the configured server, outside the workspace prefix. That is precisely the impact the diff's own comment cites as the reason to encode ids. Note the ids can no longer be used this way (they are `%2F`-escaped), so `workspace` is now the only remaining lever.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts config.workspace is interpolated raw into request URLs, but every location it cites actually encodes it. http-client.ts:100 reads `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${seg(this.config.workspace)}` — seg() is applied, not raw as claimed. The API-key routes at http-client.ts:399, :406 and :417 all use `${server}/workspaces/${seg(this.config.workspace)}/api-keys`, with :417 also seg()-encoding the key id. dry-run.ts:31 uses seg(config.workspace), and its comment at dry-run.ts:19-21 explicitly states the workspace is encoded to match HttpClient.base. api-keys.ts:16 uses seg(config.workspace), importing seg from dry-run.js at api-keys.ts:4. A repo-wide grep over packages/cli/src for 'workspaces/' and 'config.workspace' yields exactly these six production interpolations, all seg()-wrapped; the only unencoded workspace interpolations are expected-URL constants in test files (test/read-dry-run.test.ts:47,49; test/tabs.test.ts:98,153,192; test/http-client-paths.test.ts:20), which build no live requests. The doc comment at http-client.ts:28-30 names config.workspace as covered and the implementation matches it. The claimed lever therefore does not exist: WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE=ws-1/../../../admin is percent-encoded to ws-1%2F..%2F..%2F..%2Fadmin before fetch parses the URL, exactly like the document/tab/cell ids the reviewer agrees were fixed.
